extracted.intended_audience: researchers, journal editors, publishers, and research-integrity professionals
extracted.subtask_description: Identifying and responding to manipulated peer review and related research-integrity threats (paper mills, fake reviews, coordinated reviewer/editor networks) in scholarly publishing. Includes signals that indicate compromise, investigative approaches, and publisher remediation/prevention actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviews containing duplicated text
rubrics_metrics.description: Hindawi’s research integrity team found reviews that contained duplicated text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Duplicated wording across distinct review reports is a red flag for review manipulation — suggests reuse or fabrication of review content rather than independent assessments. Investigations should flag identical phrasing across reviews and compare to other submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: A few individuals doing an unusually large number of reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Investigators found 'a few individuals who did a lot of reviews.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An unusually high volume of reviews by the same reviewer(s) relative to norms for the field or journal is suspicious. Track reviewer load distributions; flag reviewers with outlier counts for further vetting (identity checks, institutional emails).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewers turning in reviews extremely quickly
rubrics_metrics.description: Some reviewers 'turned in their reviews extremely quickly.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Very rapid turnaround times (especially for complex manuscripts) can indicate cursory, non-substantive, or pre-fabricated reviews. Use expected review-time baselines per discipline; investigate outliers and request additional substantiation or re-review when suspicious.

rubrics_metrics.name: Misuse of reviewer-vetting databases
rubrics_metrics.description: Hindawi found 'misuse of databases that publishers use to vet potential reviewers.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Manipulation can include gaming reviewer-selection systems (fake profiles, hijacked identities, or misuse of third-party databases). Regular audits of suggested reviewers, email domains, and database integrity are recommended; cross-check against institutional affiliations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coordinated peer review rings (reviewers and editors colluding)
rubrics_metrics.description: The publisher suspects 'coordinated peer review rings' consisting of reviewers and editors working together to advance manuscripts through to publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for networked behavior linking reviewers and editors (repeated mutual selections, reciprocal favorable reviews, patterns across special issues). Network analysis of reviewer/editor interactions can reveal rings; treat close ties that consistently produce favorable outcomes with caution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manuscripts appearing to come from paper mills
rubrics_metrics.description: Some of the manuscripts appeared to come from paper mills.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Paper-mill output often shows repetitive phrasing, odd or irrelevant citations, improbable author affiliations or emails, and other template-driven artifacts. Combine textual analysis (e.g., 'tortured phrases'), citation patterns, and author-email checks to detect likely paper-mill products.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patterns of irregular and concerning reviewer activity across publications
rubrics_metrics.description: The team 'highlighted a pattern of irregular and concerning reviewer activity and identified potential 'bad actors' that were present across many of these publications.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presence of the same problematic reviewers/editors across multiple journals or issues strengthens evidence of systemic manipulation. Aggregate reviewer activity across a publisher's portfolio to detect cross-journal bad actors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of enhanced analytic capabilities and dashboards across reviewer activity
rubrics_metrics.description: Investigations were 'enabled by recently enhanced analytic capabilities and newly developed dashboards providing views across all reviewer activity.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Centralized analytics/dashboard tools that surface reviewer activity trends, turnaround times, review text similarities, and cross-journal links are critical detection instruments. Implement metrics and visualizations to triage suspicious cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cross-functional, combined manual and data-driven investigation
rubrics_metrics.description: Hindawi formed 'a cross-functional working team combining the manual and data-driven investigation' including research-integrity experts, data and analytics experts, publishing and operational teams, and legal counsel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Robust investigations combine quantitative analytics with human expertise and legal/operational input. Ensure multidisciplinary teams evaluate both the data indicators and the contextual evidence before action (e.g., retraction).

rubrics_metrics.name: Labeling articles as 'compromised' based on reviewer activity alone
rubrics_metrics.description: The team recommended retraction of 511 articles 'that are compromised based on reviewer activity alone.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewer-activity indicators can be sufficient grounds for considering an article compromised even if other issues (data/image fabrication) are not yet proven. Policies should specify thresholds/criteria for when reviewer-based compromise justifies retraction or correction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remedial actions: retraction, bans, institutional notification, and sharing findings
rubrics_metrics.description: The publisher plans to retract articles, has banned identified individuals, will contact research integrity officers or department heads as appropriate, and has shared its findings with industry groups and third-party databases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A multi-pronged remediation approach includes: public correction/retraction notices, banning implicated reviewers/editors from future activity, notifying employers/institutions, and sharing evidence with industry bodies/databases to prevent migration of bad actors to other journals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Holding up review/production for submissions involving potentially compromised individuals
rubrics_metrics.description: The publisher 'held up the review and production of submitted manuscripts in which "potentially compromised" individuals were involved.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quarantine or pause processing of manuscripts linked to flagged individuals until additional vetting/clean review can occur. Implement temporary holds and require independent review for such submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Industry-level collaboration and transparency as prevention
rubrics_metrics.description: Wiley/Hindawi said they will 'share our findings as transparently as possible, not just with our peers, but with industry associations, third party databases, and others' and advocated a 'cross-industry approach.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preventing migration of rings requires cross-publisher communication, shared blacklists/indicators, and coordinated industry responses. Transparency about methods and findings (appropriately redacted) facilitates collective defenses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Image duplication and doctoring as distinct integrity threats
rubrics_metrics.description: Attacks on research integrity include 'paper mills, manipulated peer review, and image duplication and doctoring.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Image forensics (duplication detection, manipulation checks) should be part of screening and post-publication review. Treat image anomalies as independent grounds for investigation and potential retraction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Community-sleuth indicators (tortured phrases, problematic paper screener, email anomalies, irrelevant citations, simultaneous submissions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Commenters noted community detection clues: 'Tortured phrases and the Problematic Paper Screener', corresponding-author email anomalies, 'meaningless irrelevant citations that occur across multiple fake papers', and 'simultaneous submission dates.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Crowdsourced signals (PubPeer comments, pattern spotting) can provide early warning. Specific flags include unusual phraseology, repeated irrelevant citation clusters across papers, non-institutional or single-use emails, and many submissions with identical or very close submission dates; follow up with formal checks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expectation that prescreening/quality checks should detect fake papers before publication
rubrics_metrics.description: Commenters argued 'Fake papers should be detected from the prescreening stage and not after publication' and questioned APCs purportedly covering 'quality checks, peer review, production and promotion.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Journals are expected to perform initial screening (scope, authorship verification, plagiarism/image checks) before peer review. Publishers should document and enforce prescreening protocols; failure to do so undermines trust and raises questions about APC-related responsibilities.
